title: Darawiish

endonym.native: Garaadada iyo suldanadii Dhulbahante ee saxiix-diidayaasha Darawiish

capsule: The Darawiish (Dervish State) was an armed Sufi resistance movement and polity in the Horn of Africa led by the poet-warrior Mohammed Abdullah Hassan, known to the British as the 'Mad Mullah,' who launched a jihad against British, Italian, and Ethiopian colonial encroachment beginning in 1899. Operating from fortified towns (including the stone fort at Taleh, built 1913–1920) in the Ogaden and Nugaal regions of present-day Somalia and Ethiopia, the movement sustained four British military expeditions between 1900 and 1904 before withdrawing to the interior. The Darawiish maintained loose political authority over the Dhulbahante and other Ogaadeen clans for over two decades before the British deployed airpower for the first time in Africa, destroying Taleh in January–February 1920; Hassan escaped but died of influenza in November 1920, ending the movement.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. The territorial extent of Darawiish control is poorly attested; the movement's reach fluctuated dramatically with military campaigns and clan allegiances, and its boundaries were never formally demarcated.
